subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Geometry — triangles, circles, coordinate geometry with visual problems

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle ABC has a right angle at C. The sides are: AC = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse AB?
questions.explanation:
Using Pythagorean theorem: AB² = AC² + BC² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. AB = √100 = 10 cm. This is the classic 6-8-10 Pythagorean triple (multiple of 3-4-5). ASCII aid:
     C
    /|
   / | 8 cm
  /  |
 A---B
  6 cm

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 7 cm. What is the area of the circle? (Use π ≈ 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area of circle = πr² = (22/7) × 7² = (22/7) × 49 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm². This is a direct formula application. Trap: students using π ≈ 3.14 but then forgetting to multiply by full r², or confusing with circumference (2πr).

questions.stem: In a triangle ABC, angle A = 60°, angle B = 50°. What is angle C?
questions.explanation: Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°. A + B + C = 180°. 60° + 50° + C = 180°. C = 180° - 110° = 70°. Fundamental geometry rule. Trap: students might forget the 180° rule or miscalculate the sum.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one of the corresponding angles is 75°, what is the measure of the other corresponding angle?
questions.explanation:
When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal. If one angle is 75°, the corresponding angle is also 75°. ASCII aid:
     Line 1 ———————
            \
             \ 75°
              \
     Line 2 ———————

Corresponding angles are equal. Trap: confusing with alternate interior angles (also equal) or co-interior angles (supplementary, sum to 180°).

questions.stem: A rectangle has length 12 cm and width 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(length + width) = 2(12 + 5) = 2 × 17 = 34 cm. ASCII aid:
┌─────────────────┐
│    12 cm        │
│                 │ 5 cm
└─────────────────┘
Perimeter = 34 cm. Trap: confusing perimeter with area (12 × 5 = 60).

questions.stem: A regular hexagon has a side length of 4 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation:
A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. Perimeter = 6 × side length = 6 × 4 = 24 cm. ASCII representation:
     ___
    /   \
   /     \
  |       |
   \     /
    \___/
Each side = 4 cm, so total = 24 cm. Trap: students might confuse with triangle (3 sides) or octagon (8 sides).

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, the sides are AB = 5 cm, BC = 12 cm, AC = 13 cm. What type of triangle is this?
questions.explanation:
Check Pythagorean theorem: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13². Since AB² + BC² = AC², triangle ABC is right-angled at B. This is the famous 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple. ASCII aid:
     C
    /|
   / | 12 cm
  /  |
 A---B
  5 cm
     13 cm (hypotenuse)
Trap: confusing which angle is 90°, or not recognizing the Pythagorean triple.
